full_text: More than one million people, predominantly women and children, are trafficked around the world each year.
subject: More than one million people

full_text: Traffickers buy young girls from relatives, kidnap children from their homes, or allure women with false promises of earning money overseas as dancers, maids, factory workers, sales clerks or models.
subject: Traffickers

full_text: Traffickers then use tactics including rape, starvation, torture, extreme physical brutality and psychological abuse to force victims to work under slavery-like conditions as prostitutes, in sweatshops, or as domestic servants.
subject: Traffickers

full_text: This legislation employs a domestic and international approach to this effort because we cannot stop trafficking into the United States if we do not address the root causes of this phenomenon in countries around the world.
subject: This legislation

full_text: The Comprehensive Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 1999 strengthens prosecution and enforcement tools against traffickers operating in the United States and expands existing services to meet the needs of domestic trafficking victims.
subject: The Comprehensive Anti-Trafficking

full_text: This legislation also works through our international affairs agencies to help other countries prevent trafficking, protect victims, and enforce their own anti-trafficking laws.
subject: This legislation

full_text: The bill creates an Inter-Agency Task Force to Monitor and Combat Trafficking, comprised of cabinet level members and chaired by the Secretary of State, and requires expanded coverage on trafficking in the annual Country Reports on Human Rights Practices.
subject: The bill

full_text: Finally, this legislation establishes a humanitarian, non-immigrant visa classification for trafficking victims in the United States and gives the President discretionary authority to impose sanctions against countries and individuals involved in trafficking.
subject: this legislation

full_text: The treatment of women incarcerated cries out for remedies.

full_text: Speaker, a battle over the budget has engulfed Congress.
subject: Speaker

full_text: Republicans made a choice to fund their own priorities, while completely ignoring the priorities of the American people, Democratic members, and the administration.
subject: Republicans

full_text: Sadly, Republicans have ignored our pleas and instead chosen to resort to name-calling and groundless accusations.
subject: Republicans

full_text: Social Security funds must be used only for Social Security.
subject: Social Security funds

full_text: These gimmicks range from declaring the 2000 census, something which happens every ten years as required by the Constitution, as emergency spending.
subject: These gimmicks

full_text: This spending dips directly into Social Security.
subject: This spending

full_text: In addition to emergency designations, Republicans have also proposed adopting a thirteen-month fiscal year, tried to withhold payment of tax credits to the working poor and ``forward-fund'' certain programs, thereby attempting to count this year's spending in next year's budget.
subject: Republicans

full_text: Rather than fulfill this promise to the people, Republicans have opted for a political showdown.
subject: Republicans

full_text: Republicans have chosen rhetoric over responsibility and taken the partisan path towards a 1.4 percent across-the-board budget cut which will have costly ramifications on critical programs.
subject: Republicans

full_text: Specifically, education for the disadvantaged would be cut by $109 million, literacy programs would be cut by $3.6 million, and Head Start would be unable to provide services to 6,700 children.
subject: literacy programs

full_text: Agricultural income assistance would be cut by $90 million, and crop and livestock loss payments would be cut by $22 million.
subject: Agricultural income assistance

full_text: In addition, national security would suffer dearly as $3.9 billion would be cut from the defense budget.
subject: national security

full_text: The men and women in the military who risk their lives for our safety and security would suffer a 2.8 percent cut in personnel.
subject: The men

full_text: As Republicans focus the energy of the Congress on their budget end game, the Patients Bill of Rights, relief for farmers and veterans' benefits face a dismal future.
subject: the Patients Bill

full_text: While Republicans devise more gimmicks to cover their tracks, Congress neglects a long overdue increase in the minimum wage, making schools safer for our children, and passing much-deserved tax relief for families, small businesses, and farmers.
subject: Congress

full_text: In a tragic example of irresponsible governance, the majority party has chosen to fund its own priorities at the cost of Social Security and drastic budget cuts in education, law enforcement, agriculture, and national security.
subject: the majority party

full_text: Speaker, as Chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, I rise today to recognize the achievements of the Hispanic Association of Colleges and Universities (HACU) National Internship Program and its federal and private-sector partners in providing Hispanic college students with invaluable real world working experiences that have allowed these students to make more educated career choices.
subject: Speaker

full_text: Over the past ten years, the HACU National Internship Program (HNIP) has introduced more than 3,800 Hispanic college students to meaningful paid internships with federal and corporate partners during the spring, summer and fall.
subject: the HACU National Internship Program

full_text: The HACU National Internship Program exposes these students to public and private sector career opportunities and specifically helps address the historic under-representation of Hispanics in the federal work force.
subject: The HACU National Internship Program

full_text: On July 10, 2002, the HACU National Internship Program will celebrate its 10th Anniversary at a ``Red, White y Azul--Investing in the American Dream,'' Gala in Washington, D.C.

full_text: This gala will showcase the achievements of former and current interns as part of a summer-long series of special events marking this remarkable program's first 10 years.
subject: This gala

full_text: The HACU National Internship program began in 1992 with 24 interns.
subject: The HACU National Internship program

full_text: In 2001 alone, the program provided paid 10- and 15-week internships to 632 interns working at 19 federal agencies and five private corporations in Washington, D.C., and at locations throughout the United States.
subject: the program

full_text: By the end of 2002, the program likely will set another record in the numbers of participating interns from throughout the country.
subject: the program

full_text: This competitive program selects top students from among HACU's 318 member and partner colleges and universities, which collectively serve more than two-thirds of all Hispanic students in higher education.
subject: This competitive program

full_text: This program provides meaningful work experiences to these students by matching their skills and career goals with the objectives of federal and corporate partners, enabling these students to make more informed career choices.
subject: This program

full_text: Based on formal program evaluations from students and supervisors, the HACU National Internship Program boasts a proven track record in positively addressing the underrepresentation of Hispanics in the federal work force.
subject: the HACU National Internship Program

full_text: Ninety-five percent of students surveyed in 2001 rated their internship experience in the federal government as ``excellent.'' More importantly, 73 percent of the 2001 summer students stated that they are interested in pursuing a career in federal service.

full_text: Of those students, 82 percent said it was a direct result of their internship experience.
subject: 82 percent

full_text: As you know, Hispanics currently comprise 11.9 percent of the civilian labor force but only 6.7 percent of the permanent federal workforce.
subject: Hispanics

full_text: As the youngest and now largest ethnic population, Hispanics already make up one of every three new workers in the overall workforce, and by 2050 are projected to make up one of every two new workers.
subject: Hispanics

full_text: Thus, the HACU National Internship Program directly addresses both the historic under-representation of Hispanics in the federal labor force and the need to address the coming shortage of public service sector employees overall.
subject: the HACU National Internship Program

full_text: In addition, this program fully supports White House Executive Order 13171, which requests that federal agencies increase their outreach to the Latino community and support programs that help address the continuing under-representation of Hispanics in federal workforce ranks.

full_text: As we all know, many employees in the service sector of the business community earn a substantial portion of their income from tips.

full_text: Recognizing this, Congress passed legislation years ago requiring employers and employees to pay FICA payroll taxes on tip income.

full_text: This legislation will remove barriers to one of the most effective preventive health screenings available, saving lives and reducing health care costs in the process.
subject: This legislation

full_text: Nearly 50,000 people will die this year from this disease.
subject: Nearly 50,000 people

full_text: According to the American Cancer Society (2009 Fact & Figures), of the nearly 50,000 people expected to die from colorectal cancer in 2009, early detection could save more than half.
subject: early detection

full_text: According to the American Cancer Society (2009 Facts & Figures), the 5 year survival rate is 90 percent for those diagnosed at an early stage; however, only 40 percent of the cases are diagnosed at the stage.
subject: only 40 percent

full_text: Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) recognizes the preventable nature of this disease and provides its only grade `A' recommendation of cancer screenings for colorectal cancer screens.
subject: Preventive Services Task Force

full_text: Unfortunately, almost half of the Medicare population is not being screened, despite the availability of a Medicare colon cancer screening benefit.
subject: almost half

full_text: Reducing Patient Barriers First, the bill would reduce patient barriers to being screened.
subject: the bill

full_text: The legislation would waive Medicare co-insurance for diagnostic and screening colorectal cancer tests in order to increase utilization.
subject: The legislation

full_text: In addition, the bill would provide coverage for a pre-operative visit with a physician prior to a screening colonoscopy.
subject: the bill

full_text: Finally, under the legislation all Medicare beneficiaries will be notified about the Medicare colorectal cancer screening benefit and reminded of the benefits periodically.
subject: all Medicare beneficiaries
object: the Medicare colorectal cancer screening benefit

full_text: The legislation reverses years of provider reimbursement cuts by creating a preventive services payment modifier for colorectal cancer screens that is adequate to incentivize physicians to perform colorectal cancer screens.
subject: The legislation

full_text: The bill would also require the Secretary to establish a national minimum standard for basic knowledge, training, continuing education and documentation for physicians and facilities.
subject: The bill

full_text: State Interventions to Increase Screening The legislation would also support state-level interventions to increase colorectal cancer screening.
subject: State Interventions

full_text: The legislation authorizes grants to states for colorectal cancer programs that include: screening to high risk individuals; case management and referrals for treatment; follow up and care for individuals screened; health professional education, training, and skills; and public information and education programs.
subject: The legislation

full_text: Information on What Works Finally, the legislation gathers information on best practices in incentivizing colorectal cancer screening.
subject: the legislation

full_text: Conclusion More than 50,000 Americans will die from colon cancer this year alone.
subject: More than 50,000 Americans

full_text: Madam Speaker, the current recession has impacted the lives of millions of American families.

full_text: Unemployment rates in the past 3 years have reached record highs, with competition for employment so steep that roughly five Americans compete for every available job.
subject: Unemployment rates

full_text: To get through these hard times, millions of unemployed Americans are raiding their retirement savings to put food on the table.
subject: millions

full_text: In 2007, over 34 million Americans participated in their employer-sponsored retirement plans, and over 20 million Americans had an Individual Retirement Account.
subject: over 34 million Americans

full_text: Unfortunately, withdrawing retirement funds early can carry stiff penalties.
subject: withdrawing

full_text: This bill will waive the penalty for such distributions made during 2009, 2010, or 2011, so long as the taxpayer received 12 consecutive weeks of unemployment compensation in the year the distribution was made.
subject: This bill

full_text: How much federal income tax people pay and what those taxes buy is not well understood by many Americans.
subject: federal income tax people

full_text: For example, a Washington Post and Kaiser Foundation poll found that by a margin of two to one, Americans believe that the federal government spends more on foreign aid than on either Social Security or Medicare.
subject: a Washington Post

full_text: This bill requires the Secretary of the Treasury to provide each taxpayer with a simple annual statement explaining how his or her federal income tax dollars were spent.
subject: This bill

full_text: Similar to the annual Social Security statement, the Taxpayer Receipt will show the taxpayer's income tax liability, the amount of the liability spent on major spending categories, and the actual federal outlays for each category.
subject: the Taxpayer Receipt

full_text: This simple annual Taxpayer Receipt will provide clear and consistent information to taxpayers that will serve to educate taxpayers on government spending--a subject full of misinformation.
subject: This simple annual Taxpayer Receipt

full_text: Madam Speaker, today, I introduce the Low-Wage Federal Contractor Employee Back Pay Act to grant back pay to federally contracted retail, food, custodial and security service workers who are furloughed during the current and any other federal government shutdown this fiscal year (fiscal year 2019).

full_text: This bill applies to all three branches of the federal government.
subject: This bill

full_text: After government shutdowns, federal workers have received back pay, but not federal contract workers, who often perform the same jobs as civil servants.
subject: federal workers

full_text: Therefore, my bill focuses specifically on low-wage federal contract workers, some of whom work here on the [[Page E21]] Capitol Grounds providing Members of Congress and congressional staff with daily services, because these are the workers most likely to be irretrievably hurt by lost wages during a shutdown.
subject: my bill

full_text: Madam Speaker, today, I introduce the Northern Mariana Islands Small Business Act, which would ensure small businesses in my district have access to the Small Business Administration's (SBA) Small Business Development Center (SBDC) Lead Center grant program, the Federal and State Technology (FAST) partnership grant program and the Microloan program.

full_text: For a century, the men and women of the 103d Attack Squadron have served our nation with distinction, dedication, resilience, and valor.
